checks.title: Complete the interaction by keyboard
checks.steps: Use Tab/Shift+Tab and the documented activation keys. Complete and recover from the task without a pointer.
checks.expected: All controls remain reachable and operable.

checks.title: Inspect visible focus
checks.steps: Move through each interactive control; inspect the focus indication and whether content obscures it.
checks.expected: The current focus remains visibly identifiable.

checks.title: Understand field errors
checks.steps: Submit invalid synthetic values, locate the errors, correct them, and resubmit.
checks.expected: Each error is associated with its field and recovery preserves other values.

checks.title: Understand modal context
checks.steps: Using the chosen assistive technology, open the dialog and inspect its name, content context, dismissal and focus return.
checks.expected: The user can understand the dialog and return to the invoking context.

checks.title: Discover and operate the action menu
checks.steps: Locate the menu button, open it, navigate commands, activate and dismiss.
checks.expected: State, navigation and action feedback are understandable.

checks.title: Inspect zoom and reflow
checks.steps: Inspect at 320 CSS pixels and, when possible, actual browser zoom at 200 percent.
checks.expected: Content and actions remain usable; note browser zoom separately from viewport emulation.

checks.title: Inspect reduced-motion behavior
checks.steps: Enable the operating-system/browser reduced-motion preference and repeat the interaction.
checks.expected: Nonessential movement is removed and feedback remains understandable.

checks.title: Assess spoken interaction feedback
checks.steps: Record an actual human assistive-technology session for field errors, dialog or action feedback.
checks.expected: Expected feedback is understandable in the recorded AT/browser combination.
